licence.title: Physician Assistant (supervised or collaborative licence)
licence.renewalDeadline: March 1 of the year following expiration of NCCPA (or board-approved) certification; late renewal with fees until June 1, then lapsed

ce.categoryRules: No separate state CME hour count; current NCCPA (or board-approved certifying agency) certification is required at each renewal

topicMandates.topic: Pain management and prescribing of controlled substances
topicMandates.appliesTo: PAs holding federal DEA and New Mexico controlled substances registrations; may also count toward NCCPA
licensees with DEA and NM CS registration, during the first year of licensure

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 3 hours pain management every biennial cycle for DEA plus NM CS registrants; 5 hours in first year of licensure

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Supervising physician files written notice of intent to supervise on board forms; the PA renews the registration of supervision with the board every two years along with the licence (NMSA 61-6C-3(F)); notice to the board within 30 days after an employer ends a PA's employment. Collaborative status available (primary care, 3 years supervised practice, malpractice insurance, current NCCPA).
practice.notes: Two tracks: supervised PA (direction via written utilization plan or direct communication, QA program) and collaborative PA for primary care after three years. No renewal cadence for the supervision form found in rule.

prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 3 hours pain management per biennial cycle (5 hours first year) for DEA plus NM CS registrants

aprn.title: CNP (Certified Nurse Practitioner) licence

unverified: 16.10.15 and 16.10.14 NMAC (PA) were read from the SRCA compilation (latest history 2/8/2022). NMMB's own rules page still posts the 2022-02-08 versions as current. No later NM Register amendment was found, but the Register itself was not searched.

The NM PA Act was read from the scanned NMMB PDF (Westlaw print current through the 2023 session) using OCR. Both 2025 and 2026 bills to change PA supervision died. No other 2024 to 2026 session law amending 61-6C was checked.

Whether a collaborative PA must file a written collaboration agreement with the board: 16.10.15 NMAC and NMSA 61-6C-3(G) require only a 'supervising or collaborating relationship'. No filing rule was found.
NM PA: no state CME hour count beyond NCCPA certification and the controlled substance pain hours. The app should treat NCCPA status as the general CME mechanism.
The NM Board of Pharmacy controlled substance registration renewal period (16.19.20 NMAC) could not be read clearly from the SRCA page. Left unconfirmed.

NM CNP: national certification meets the CE requirement under 16.12.17.9(A)(3)(a). Whether the board still applies the RN 30-hour count to an APRN holding only a single-state RN licence was not confirmed beyond that sentence.

Checked 16.12.16, 16.12.17 and 16.10.14/15 NMAC and found no topic mandate on implicit bias, human trafficking, child abuse, HIV, Alzheimer, suicide prevention, infection control, cultural competency or domestic violence for PAs or NPs.

corrections: NM PA: the supervision registration renews every two years with the licence (NMSA 1978, 61-6C-3(F), PA Act PDF on nmmb.state.nm.us). The researcher had listed this cadence as unknown.
NM PA: confirmed on nmlegis.gov that 2026 HB150 and 2025 HB267 both died, so PA supervision law is unchanged. NMMB still posts the 16.10.14 and 16.10.15 NMAC versions dated 2022-02-08 as current.

NM NP: 16.12.2 NMAC is REPEALED. The NM Board of Nursing replaced it on January 1, 2026 with 16.12.16 NMAC (RN), 16.12.17 NMAC (APRN) and a replaced 16.12.9 NMAC (pain). The researcher cited 16.12.2 from the stale SRCA compilation. Every NP fact is re-cited to the current rule PDFs on files.bon.nm.gov.

NM NP: the RN rule's 'certification accepted in lieu of the 30 hours' sentence was removed. New 16.12.16.11(E) says only that certification 'may be used as an approved CE'. For APRNs, 16.12.17.9(A)(3)(a) now says national certification 'meets the requirement for RN and APRN continuing education'.
NM NP: removed the CNP 'maintain a formulary with each renewal' fact. The CNP section of the current 16.12.17.14 NMAC has no formulary requirement; only CRNAs keep one (16.12.17.15).
